scenes.heading: DNA manipulation techniques
scenes.sub: Cut, paste, copy and sort DNA
scenes.say: How do scientists solve crimes from a single hair, or get bacteria to make human insulin? They cut DNA at exact places, join pieces, make millions of copies, and sort fragments by size. Let's see how.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Find, cut and paste when you edit text on your phone
scenes.science: Restriction enzymes find and cut a site; DNA ligase pastes
scenes.breaks: your phone can search any phrase, but each restriction enzyme only recognises its own short sequence (usually 4–8 base pairs).
scenes.say: Think of find, cut and paste on your phone. A restriction enzyme searches DNA for one exact recognition site and cuts there every time. DNA ligase is the paste and save. It seals the backbone so the join is permanent.

scenes.heading: Sticky vs blunt ends
scenes.say: A staggered cut leaves sticky ends: short overhangs that base-pair like Velcro. Cut two samples with the same enzyme and their sticky ends match. A straight cut leaves blunt ends, which can join any blunt end, but less efficiently.

scenes.heading: PCR: hot, cold, warm
scenes.say: PCR copies a target section of DNA. Remember hot, cold, warm. Heat to about ninety-five degrees to split the strands. Cool to about fifty-five so primers stick. Warm to seventy-two so Taq polymerase builds new strands. Each cycle doubles the copies.
scenes.caption: PCR copies a target section of DNA. Remember hot, cold, warm. Heat to about 95 °C to split the strands. Cool to about 55 °C so primers stick. Warm to 72 °C so Taq polymerase builds new strands. Each cycle doubles the copies.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Starting with 3 copies of a target, how many copies are present after 10 cycles of PCR?
scenes.say: Start with three copies and run ten cycles. Copies equal three times two to the power of ten. That's three times one thousand and twenty-four, which gives three thousand and seventy-two copies.
scenes.caption: Start with 3 copies and run 10 cycles. Copies = 3 × 2¹⁰. That's 3 × 1024, which gives 3072 copies.

scenes.heading: Gel electrophoresis
points: DNA is negative, so it runs to the positive end
Large fragments stay near the wells
Compare bands with a DNA ladder
scenes.say: Gel electrophoresis sorts DNA by size. DNA is negatively charged, so it runs to the positive electrode. Run to red! Small fragments slip through the gel and travel further. Compare your bands with a DNA ladder to estimate their size.

scenes.heading: CRISPR and DNA profiling
points: Guide RNA leads Cas9 to cut a chosen gene
One STR band from each parent
scenes.say: CRISPR began as a bacterial defence. Scientists now design a guide RNA to lead Cas9 to cut any gene they choose. DNA profiling compares short tandem repeats, which vary between people. You get one version from each parent, so a child's bands must all come from the mother or father.

points: Restriction enzymes cut at recognition sites
scenes.say: Quick recap. Restriction enzymes cut, ligase pastes. PCR doubles DNA every cycle. Gels sort fragments by size, with small ones travelling furthest. And STR profiles identify people. Now try the practice questions!
